title: Mammatus Clouds
content: Before the big thunderstorm arrived last Tuesday night, I sat outside and sketched some strange cloud formations.They're called mammatus clouds, named so because their pendulous forms resemble an animal's udder or a woman's breasts. They are found at the base of anvil clouds, the giant cumulonimbus clouds that generate extreme thunderstorms.As I made this quick notation with my water brushes, the wind whipped the treetops. The clouds swirled and turned green. Big raindrops started falling around me. I folded up my sketch gear and retreated indoors. Hail pounded the deck outside. Lightning flashed, then thunder. Suddenly the electric power died and stayed out for several hours.I finished the sketch by the light of a kerosene lantern.Mammatus clouds on Wikipedia
